title: A bill to establish the Department of Artificial Intelligence and to provide for the regulation of advanced artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new Department of Artificial Intelligence to oversee the development and deployment of advanced AI systems. It also establishes regulatory frameworks to ensure those systems operate safely, ethically, and transparently, while setting up mechanisms for oversight and enforcement.

title: A bill to require disclosure of certain information relating to artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill mandates that organizations using or deploying AI systems must disclose certain key information about those systems. It also includes other related provisions to promote transparency and accountability in AI development and use.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.
summary: The Senate emphasizes that religious freedom must be protected even as AI systems become more widespread. It also calls for the use of authoritative texts and demands greater transparency in the development and deployment of AI.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 aims to ensure AI tools used in veteran services are safe, fair, and accountable. It proposes oversight mechanisms, transparency requirements, and protections to prevent bias and misuse while benefiting veterans.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act proposes stricter controls on artificial intelligence systems to prevent harmful or unregulated behavior. It aims to establish oversight mechanisms and enforce safety standards, ensuring AI development remains aligned with societal values.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is designed to ensure that any AI systems used in processing veterans’ benefits claims operate fairly, transparently, and with clear responsibility. It establishes guidelines and oversight mechanisms so that the decisions made by these AI tools can be tracked, audited, and corrected if necessary.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a proposed law that bans certain uses of artificial intelligence that are considered harmful or disallowed. It would forbid the development, deployment, or commercial use of these specified AI applications and impose penalties for violations.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act requires that all AI systems used in defense be rigorously tested to meet strict reliability and safety standards before they can be deployed. It also mandates regular reporting and monitoring of AI behavior to ensure transparency, accountability, and continued compliance with national security and safety requirements.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how it uses artificial intelligence and to make information about the underlying algorithms and decision‑making processes publicly available. The law is designed to promote accountability and protect veterans by ensuring they can understand and trust the AI systems that affect their care and benefits.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a pilot program that uses AI to strengthen cyber defenses for critical infrastructure. It also outlines additional measures to protect essential services and infrastructure from evolving cyber threats.

title: To establish a human-centered Federal framework for artificial intelligence in education and the workforce, promote the ethical and responsible teaching and learning of artificial intelligence, provide for equitable access to artificial intelligence-ready workforce development, safeguard student and worker data privacy, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy aims to create a human‑centered federal framework for using AI in education and the workforce, emphasizing ethical and responsible teaching and learning. It also seeks to ensure equitable access to AI‑ready workforce development, protect student and worker data privacy, and address related goals.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a proposed law aimed at strengthening the security of artificial intelligence systems. It sets out guidelines and standards for identifying, mitigating, and responding to AI‑related risks to protect users and critical infrastructure.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act is a proposed law that prohibits the use of artificial intelligence to automatically reject Medicare claims. It requires that any denial must involve a human review and provide clear explanations to protect beneficiaries from opaque algorithmic decisions.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: An AI Data Center Moratorium Act would halt the construction and operation of new AI data centers for a specified period. The goal is to reduce environmental impact, limit energy consumption, and encourage more sustainable technology practices.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act seeks to stop companies from charging excessively high prices for AI services and from setting fixed wages that disadvantage workers in the AI sector. It proposes rules and enforcement mechanisms to ensure fair pricing and to protect employees from wage manipulation in the rapidly growing AI industry.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is designed to stop the illegal copying and misuse of AI models in the United States by tightening legal safeguards and increasing penalties for theft. The act also calls for stronger cooperation between AI developers, law‑enforcement agencies, and industry groups to monitor and protect intellectual property in AI technology.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 sets up a framework for studying and monitoring how artificial intelligence is used in judicial settings, aiming to ensure fair, accurate, and accountable court processes. It establishes dedicated research bodies and oversight mechanisms to evaluate AI tools, address bias concerns, and maintain public trust in the legal system.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 is a law that sets rules for how the Small Business Administration can use artificial intelligence tools. It aims to ensure AI is employed responsibly, protects privacy, and supports innovation while complying with federal standards.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act seeks to shield individuals from misleading or false information generated by artificial intelligence. It sets out rules that require companies to be transparent, provide clear disclosure, and maintain accountability for AI-produced content so consumers can make informed choices.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act aims to put the U.S. federal government at the forefront of AI development and to create a single, nationwide set of rules for AI technology. It seeks to coordinate regulations, boost innovation, and protect national security by ensuring consistent standards across the country.

title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that establishes a framework for managing and mitigating the risks associated with artificial intelligence technologies. It requires federal agencies to conduct risk assessments, set safety standards, and enforce oversight to ensure AI systems are designed, deployed, and monitored in ways that protect public safety and privacy.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act aims to foster the adoption of artificial intelligence technologies within the banking, investment, and insurance sectors. It establishes guidelines to encourage innovation while ensuring consumer protection, data privacy, and regulatory compliance.

title: HBCU AI Research Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The HBCU AI Research Leadership Act is intended to boost AI research at historically black colleges and universities by providing funding, resources, and support for labs and programs. It also promotes partnerships with industry and other institutions to increase diversity and create a more inclusive AI workforce.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a legislative proposal aimed at integrating AI education into primary and secondary schools. It seeks to equip students with the knowledge and skills necessary to understand and responsibly use artificial intelligence technologies.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard consumers against misleading AI-generated content by requiring transparency and honesty in AI communications. It establishes guidelines and penalties to ensure that AI products cannot deceive users about their nature, capabilities, or data usage.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act establishes a legal framework for the responsible development and deployment of AI models, setting standards for safety, transparency, and accountability. It requires developers to conduct rigorous testing, provide clear documentation, and comply with regulatory oversight to protect users and society from potential harms associated with AI systems.

title: SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Small Business.
summary: The SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026 requires the Small Business Administration to collect and publish data on how small businesses are adopting AI technologies. The act is intended to increase transparency, help shape policy, and support responsible AI use within the small‑business community.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed U.S. law designed to regulate artificial intelligence systems, emphasizing safety, transparency, and accountability. It likely includes rules for risk assessment, mandatory disclosures, and oversight to protect consumers and prevent misuse of AI technology.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 seeks to make companies responsible for the decisions made by their AI systems by requiring regular audits for fairness, bias, and privacy. It establishes reporting, oversight, and penalty mechanisms to ensure algorithmic transparency and protect citizens from discriminatory or harmful automated decisions.
